title: Capacity slab pricing, negotiated SLA bands, and security questionnaire onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Produce a negotiable capacity slab pricing blueprint for Dedicated (reserved GPUs) that combines clear SLA bands, burst credit mechanics, and an onboarding pack for enterprise security questionnaires (SQ). Deliverables: 1) Pricing slabs & example contracts with throughput guarantees (slots/lanes) and overage mechanics; 2) Burst credit model and policy for transient demand with clear accounting; 3) Autoscale guardrails for reserved pools, preemption rules, and billing reconciliation; 4) A fillable SQ bundle (answers + evidence links) tailored to pricing tiers for sales/legal to attach to RFPs. Background: Sales repeatedly requests an off-the-shelf negotiable structure that reduces back-and-forth in enterprise procurement while protecting margins and capacity predictability. Engineering needs guardrails to avoid noisy autoscale behavior and to prevent SLA exposure in multi-tenant Dedicated clusters. Workstreams: - Pricing: define 4 slab levels (mini, standard, guaranteed, enterprise-lane) with step-up discounts and SLAs mapped to p99 latency & throughput units. - Burst: define credit bucket sizing, expiration, replenishment cadence and hard caps per customer. - Autoscale & Preemption: policies for opportunistic slots, graceful fallback to host models, backfill windows. - SQ Onboarding: craft templated answers for common security questionnaire items (networking, KMS, audit logs, breach notification) and attach artifacts (audit report excerpt, diagram). Key trade-offs: - Simplicity vs granularity: more slab granularity reduces negotiation friction for mid-market but increases billing complexity. - Tight SLAs raise price; offering multi-tier SLA with fallback model variants preserves availability but requires observable fallbacks in Console. - Burst generosity improves sales motion but increases short-term capacity risk; mitigations include burst caps, smoothing windows, and surge pricing. Success criteria: - Sales can close 3 pilot enterprise PO/SLAs with new structure within 6 weeks. - Engineering implements autoscale guardrails and a billing reconciliation test harness. - Legal & Security sign off on SQ bundle and artifact links. Artifacts and links: - Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DED/pages/Capacity+Slab+Design - Pricing spreadsheet (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-pricing-spreadsheet - Draft contract template (Drive): https://drive.google.com/file/draft-contract-example.pdf - SQ bundle (shared folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-sq-bundle - Dashboard prototype (internal): https://internal.redwood.ai/dedicated/pricing-simulator - GitHub PR (billing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/892 - GitHub PR (autoscale): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2145

notes_for_sales: Include estimator example: Standard slab (8 GPUs) + 1 month burst (2000 credit units) -> expected blended unit cost X. For enterprise lanes, show p99 SLAs and sample credit cap ranges. Always attach SQ bundle and contract template. Use trial lane for POC conversions.
